messages:
aj: Quick kickoff — we need to finalize the SDK+docs gating matrix for the next feature wave. My proposal: categorize features into MUST / SHOULD / NICE-TO-HAVE for the initial rollout and map owners + exact launch criteria. Focus areas: structured output (typed schemas), function/tool-calling, rerank+embeddings pipeline, and canonical examples + changelog cadence. Who wants to pick preferred must-haves?

maria: I vote structured output (order/invoice schemas) and function-calling as MUST. AcmeRetail is blocking until we have typed order confirmations they can validate. Also need a small test harness for schema regression tests.

sophia: Agree with maria. Proposed gating columns: API parity, SDK types (py/ts), canonical examples, migration guide, changelog entry, security review, CI smoke tests, perf regression. Suggest we set a 2-week alpha/internal preview after those gates pass.

ian: From runtime side: confirm streaming + KV cache behavior for function-calling and structured outputs. We need compatibility tests for streaming partial structured outputs — a few models behave differently. I can add a CI job to run against the nightly runtime images. Also +1 on feature flags so infra can toggle new behavior.

ryan: Docs notes: canonical examples should be minimal runnable snippets (one-liners where possible) and a longer example that demonstrates an embeddings->rerank flow. I'll own TS examples if someone pairs on Python. Also: changelog cadence — we should publish a single rollout changelog per minor release and a short migration guide for breaking changes.

sam: Customer success input: two enterprise accounts asked for an embeddings->rerank sample that shows cost/perf tradeoffs. They want an estimate script to show token/embedding cost comparisons. Please include a sample cost calc in examples.

maria: Example typed interface (TS) for order confirmation — want parity in Python.

```ts
// canonical minimal example
import {RedwoodClient}from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY});

const resp = await client.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-chat-1',
  messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Confirm order #12345'}],
  structured_output: {
    schema: {type: 'object', properties: {order_id: {type: 'string'}, total: {type: 'number'}}}
  }
});
console.log(resp.structured_output);
```

ryan: That snippet looks good. For docs we should show both the raw JSON response and the typed interface. I'll draft the TypeScript example and a python equivalent.

aj: Proposed decisions so far (please react):
- MUST: structured_output typed schemas, function/tool-calling (basic sync+async), SDK typed interfaces for Python + TS, canonical examples for each surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank), migration guide, changelog entry, CI smoke tests.
- SHOULD: embeddings->rerank sample + cost script, streaming partial-structure handling, automated evals for quality regressions.
- NICE-TO-HAVE: advanced structured validation UI in console, per-route schema enforcement.

aj: Owners & timeline (alpha target in 3 weeks):
- Structured types + schema regression harness — maria (eng-ml)
- Function/tool calling parity tests — ian (runtime)
- Canonical examples & changelog — ryan (docs) + maria (examples)
- Migration guide + SDK release notes — sophia (product)
- CI smoke jobs + feature flags — ian

aj: Please +1 or :thumbsup: or comment with objections by EOD Friday. If no blockers, I'll lock the matrix and open GH issues.

devex-bot: CI: nightly-compat-tests started against runtime-nightly-2026-03-21 (job #4721) — will post results to the thread when finished.

maria: One blocker note: we need a short deprecation window documented if field names change — propose 90 days for breaking schema changes and a compat shim in SDKs.

sophia: 90 days sounds reasonable. Add a checklist item: "deprecation note + compat shim" before marking release GA.

ian: Quick FYI on streaming: some models stream text tokens but not structured output chunks. I'll add a CI case that asserts the structured schema is emitted in full or provides a clean error path.

ryan: I'll start drafting the docs PR and the canonical examples repo branch. Tagging @maria for schema ownership so examples reference the authoritative specs.

aj: Thanks everyone — I'll create the gating matrix doc and break out GH issues with owners tonight.

sam: Adding one more customer ask: please include an example that shows how to verify signatures/HMAC on function outputs for high security customers. They called that a must for FedRAMP prospects.

maria: Good call — adding HMAC verification snippet to examples.

aj: Noted. Locking in owners unless anyone objects. Final sign-off needed by Friday. :calendar:
